questions.key_step: Differentiation of $(x^2-2x)\sin x$ recognised, or two parts integrations.
questions.justification: Short separable DE; the only work is integration by parts or spotting the exact derivative. MCQ options help.

questions.key_step: Simplify $\sin x(\sec x-\sin x\tan x)=\sin x\cos x$, then I.F. $\cot x$.
questions.justification: Algebraic simplification, then a routine linear DE with a $\csc 2x$ integral; standard but with several steps.

questions.key_step: Put $x=vy$ and separate.
questions.justification: Textbook homogeneous DE with a log; one substitution then $\int\frac{dv}{v\ln v}$.

questions.key_step: Substitute $t=x+y$ then $z=t^2$ and partial fractions.
questions.justification: Non-obvious substitution plus a cubic-to-quadratic reduction and a precise final evaluation; options help.

questions.key_step: Show the given data are contradictory.
questions.justification: Solving is trivial; the idea is to notice that the limit condition and the sign of $\alpha$ conflict (bonus question).

questions.key_step: I.F. $\sqrt{1-x^2}$ gives an exact derivative.
questions.justification: Routine linear DE with an unusual radical integrating factor and clean final fraction; numerical answer, no options.

questions.key_step: Multiply $f''=f$ by $f'$ and integrate.
questions.justification: One idea (first integral) then $\sinh^{-1}$ integral; the data ($f$ odd, $f'\ge0$) are decoration.

questions.key_step: I.F. $e^{2\tan x}$ then $\int e^{2u}(2+3u)du$ by parts.
questions.justification: Standard linear DE with a trig I.F.; a single by-parts and arithmetic.

questions.key_step: I.F. $\sqrt{1-x^2}$ then odd/even split and a standard $\int\frac{x^2}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}$.
questions.justification: Linear DE then a definite integral using symmetry and a trig integral: two linked skills with exact surd answer.

questions.key_step: Differentiate the integral equation to get $(x+2)f'-3f=3$.
questions.justification: Leibniz differentiation then a separable DE; the initial value comes from the original equation.

questions.key_step: I.F. $\sec^2x$ and $\int\sec x\tan x\,dx$.
questions.justification: Routine linear DE with trig functions; evaluation at two points is mechanical.

questions.key_step: $t=\sin^{-1}\frac x2$ gives I.F. $e^{t^2/2}$, then by parts.
questions.justification: Needs the inverse-trig substitution twice and a by-parts with an exponential of $t^2$; longer but standard.

questions.key_step: I.F. $e^{-x}$ and $\int e^{-x}\sin x\,dx$.
questions.justification: Routine linear DE; one standard integral and a clean condition.

questions.key_step: $t=x+y+2$ gives $t'=1+t^2$; monotonic so extremes at ends.
questions.justification: Easy substitution and a monotonicity step, followed by surd algebra.

questions.key_step: The limit is $2xf-x^2f'$, giving a linear DE.
questions.justification: Limit-definition turns into a DE like the 2024 anchor; solve with I.F. $x^{-2}$ and evaluate at two points.

questions.key_step: I.F. makes $f'=x$; then the area of a parabola segment.
questions.justification: Linear DE whose integral collapses immediately, then a routine area; no trap.

questions.key_step: Tangent-slope condition gives a parabola; focal distance.
questions.justification: Two chapters (DE and conics) with a disguised parabola; separable DE is easy but the identification and focus step add length.

questions.key_step: Separate variables.
questions.justification: One-step separable DE and a trivial evaluation.

questions.key_step: Divide by $xy$ to see exact differentials.
questions.justification: Requires spotting $d(xy)$ and $d\ln|y/x|$ and the uniqueness of $\alpha,\beta$; idea availability moderate.

questions.key_step: Equilibrium value $-\frac\alpha3$ from the limit.
questions.justification: Simple linear DE; the limit condition fixes $\alpha$; a short computation.
